title: Feature Settings — General tab
description: Account-level General settings: User activation toggle and the Guides, tutorials & announcements feature with user-deployment management.

designSystem.name: Spring UI (tokens + icons; components are Spring-styled Tailwind/Radix equivalents)

targets.title: General tab — settings list
targets.description: Two setting cards under the Feature Settings heading and pill tabs.

hierarchy: Pill tab row: General (selected), Phone, AI, SMS, Fax
SettingCard “User activation” — icon, description with Learn more link, switch (off by default)
SettingCard “Guides, tutorials & announcements” — switch (on), summary pills “User default: On” / “User access: Allowed”, Manage button
elements.layout: Cards are full-width flex rows with 16px padding, 8px radius, 1px neutral-b4 border, stacked with 16px gap inside the tab shell (flex-1 next to a 190px side nav in a 1200px frame).
elements.styling: Spring tokens via CSS variables: text neutral-b1/b2, primary-b for links and switch-on, neutral-b5 summary pills (32px tall, 10px radius).
elements.content: Copy is exactly as coded in GeneralPanel.tsx; all data is mock store state.

responsive.behavior: Fixed 1200px centered frame; pill tabs wrap with flex-wrap; no dedicated mobile layout.

states.description: Three 120px-tall pulsing slate skeleton bars replace the panel for ~250ms after every tab activation (FeatureSettings.tsx).
When Guides is off its summary pills and Manage remain but Manage is disabled at 50% opacity; switch shows unchecked.

localInteractions.outcome: Opens the matching confirm/enable dialog instead of toggling immediately.
A top-center toast (“Settings were updated.” or “<Feature> turned on/off”) appears with an Undo action that reverts the last snapshot.

integrationBoundaries.productionOwns: persisting feature settings, error handling, and undo semantics
integrationBoundaries.prototypeAssumption: All changes mutate an in-memory reducer store; Undo restores a single snapshot; a simulateError flag fakes save failures.
integrationBoundaries.productionQuestion: Use the repository’s existing settings persistence, error handling, and undo/rollback approach.

integrationBoundaries.productionOwns: real per-feature user override counts and org user totals
integrationBoundaries.prototypeAssumption: Counts such as “26/98 users” are mock constants seeded in the store.
integrationBoundaries.productionQuestion: Resolve counts from the production user-settings service.

acceptance: General pill is selected on load and the two cards render in order.
Guides card shows both summary pills and an enabled Manage button while on.
Switch clicks never toggle silently — a dialog always intercepts.

targets.title: User activation on/off confirm dialog
targets.description: 600px SpringConfirmDialog. Title/body/confirm label swap between turn-on and turn-off copy based on current state.

states.description: Title “Turn on User activation for your organization?”; confirm “Turn on”.
Title “Turn off…”; body warns users can’t re-generate activation email; confirm “Turn off”.

localInteractions.outcome: Dispatches the toggle, closes, shows undo toast.

actions: Click the User activation card switch
activationRecipe.expected: The confirm dialog is open with turn-on copy (default state is off).

acceptance: Copy variant matches the current switch state.

targets.title: Guides enable / disable / manage dialogs
targets.description: Three flows on the Guides card: disable confirm (SpringConfirmDialog), enable dialog (SpringFeatureEnableDialog with user-deployment options and custom-users decision when customUsers > 0), and Manage dialog (SpringFeatureManageDialog with User default On/Off and User access checkbox).

hierarchy: Enable/Manage: title, deployment radio/selects, custom-users section (26 users seeded)
elements.styling: Error state renders a red-50 banner “Couldn’t save settings. Try again.” and the primary button reads Retry.

states.description: “Turn off … for your organization?” with restore note.
Deployment options + “26 users have custom settings” decision.
Current default/access values editable; Save commits and toasts.
With store simulateError on, Save shows the red banner and Retry; the retry click clears the simulated error.

integrationBoundaries.productionOwns: real per-feature user override counts and org user totals
integrationBoundaries.prototypeAssumption: Counts such as “26/98 users” are mock constants seeded in the store.
integrationBoundaries.productionQuestion: Resolve counts from the production user-settings service.

actions: Click Manage on the Guides card
activationRecipe.expected: Manage dialog open with User default: On, User access: Allowed.

acceptance: Turning Guides off requires the confirm; turning on opens the enable dialog with the custom-users decision.

flows.title: Toggle a General feature
flows.notes: Every switch interaction routes through a dialog before the store changes; a toast with Undo follows every commit.

acceptedDeviations.requirement: Keep the prototype’s Spring-styled Tailwind + Radix primitives (SettingCard, SpringSwitch, SpringConfirmDialog, etc.); @ringcentral/spring-ui is not installed and the task forbids redesigning the finalized UI.
Keep lucide-react utility glyphs (close X, chevrons, search, info) inside dialogs/controls; visual parity with the approved prototype takes precedence.
Keep Tailwind default-palette utilities used for the loading skeleton (slate-100), error banners (red-50/red-800), overlays (black/40) and white surfaces.
Admin Portal chrome (masthead, side nav, footer) intentionally uses the legacy Service Web UI palette (#0679BA, #2F2F2F, #FBFBFB…) scoped under .swui-scope, not Spring tokens.

sourceClosureNote: The app is a single SPA: src/App.tsx statically imports FeatureSettings.tsx, which statically imports all five tab panels and the AI helper modules. sourceFiles therefore lists the full transitive import graph — identical for every feature — so any manifest alone is a complete, buildable source set. Files primary to this feature carry feature-specific descriptions; the rest are marked (shared closure).
